lines.text: true that what we consider the abnormal and disturbing,
what, we suppose, really ought not to be, is precisely the
kind of crisis in which we catch a glimpse of true and
essential being, of the innermost reality of life?
In the life of every man eternity finally intrudes in the
form of death. Death stands at the door and knocks some
time or other for all of us. The popular legend speaks with
deep truth about the messengers of death whom the latter
sends in advance to warn people of its imminent approach.
These messengers are pain and sorrow, old age and other
tokens of our transience. Shall we frivolously disregard them?
Or shall we pay heed to them and prepare ourselves for the
coming of eternity? Is it not the messengers of death, of
eternity, which bring us back to ourselves? Especially is
sorrow meant to bring us to ourselves and to enable us to
receive that gold which is refined with fire. "Those whom
I love, I reprove and chasten; so be zealous and repent."
Yet it would be wrong to think that only pain and the
signs of our transitoriness were the messengers of eternity.
There are indeed other messengers and with the blindness of
our ingratitude we fail to notice them. They are all the
pleasing and cheering things which are sent to us to give us
joy. It may be every beam of morning sunlight, every flower
which delights us with its beauty and fragrance, every look
of love, every kind gift which comes our way. Of course all
these things have to be rightly understood and rightly
received if they are to be for us messengers of eternity. If
ungratefully we take all this happiness and joy for granted
as something which we deserve, then we do not understand
the message of these things, which is that what gives purest
joy and deepest happiness to our lives is always a wondrous
gift, a sheer marvel.
If we fail to open our hearts to these small occasions of
happiness, or if we allow the moments or hours of blessing
to fade away without response, without really taking them to
ourselves by an impulse of grateful acceptance, then they
lose their meaning for us and our souls remain empty. If on
